summary.A: LB rules (DAMOS only) classify 3 of 12 anchors as place-like (PA-I-TO, SE-TO-I-JA, SU-KI-RI-TA), 2 as person-like (I-TA-JA, PA-RA-NE), 7 unclear. Linear A has 4 place-anchor tokens and 3 person-anchor tokens. No feature separates them beyond matched random words (all p>0.2 with label permutation; minimum attainable label-permutation p with 5 types is 0.1). Adding the 2-sign matches (7 place, 9 person types) also gives no significant feature (all p>=0.13). Verdict: no detectable place-slot vs person-slot distinction; test underpowered.
summary.B: Productive beyond random-sign control: A- (11 vs 3.4, p<0.001), I- (8 vs 3.4, p=0.02), -JA (7 vs 3.1, p=0.03); -ME and -TE marginal (p~0.07-0.10); SI-, KI-, -RE not; JA- only via A-/JA- alternation. Register tie: -TE, -ME and JA- forms sit on stone/metal objects and vessels, not tablets (token p<0.001; type level p=0.012-0.07), versus random-sign forms on the same stems (0.17-0.27 objects). SI- forms always carry a number (6/6 types, type p=0.006). -RE with "1" (type p=0.02) does not survive ~99 comparisons. Hold-out (fit on Hagia Triada, test elsewhere): 1 hit of 94 predicted forms (A-MI-TA at Zakros), vs 0.43 random-sign control, p=0.35. Verdict: affixes real; paradigm table does not predict unseen forms.
